verses.zh: 大流士王第二年六月初一日，耶和华的话藉先知哈该向犹大省长撒拉铁的儿子所罗巴伯和约撒答的儿子大祭司约书亚说：
verses.en: On the first day of the sixth month[NOTE:1] of King Darius’[NOTE:2] second year, the Lord’s message came through[NOTE:3] the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak:[NOTE:4]
notes: The first day of the sixth month was Elul 1 according to the Jewish calendar; August 29, 520 b.c. according to the modern (Julian) calendar.
King Darius is the Persian king Darius Hystaspes who ruled from 522-486 b.c.
Heb “by the hand of.” This suggests that the prophet is only an instrument of the Lord; the Lord is to be viewed as the true author (see 1:3; 2:1; Mal 1:1).

The typical translation “Joshua (the) son of Jehozadak, the high priest” (cf. ASV, NASB, NIV, NRSV) can be understood to mean that Jehozadak was high priest. However, Zech 3:1, 8 clearly indicate that Joshua was high priest (see also Ezra 5:1-2; cf. NAB). The same potential misunderstanding occurs in Hag 1:12, 14 and 2:2, where the same solution has been employed in the translation.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：「这百姓说，建造耶和华殿的时候尚未来到。」
verses.en: This is what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] has said: “These people have said, ‘The time for rebuilding the Lord’s temple has not yet come.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: The epithet Lord of Heaven’s Armies occurs frequently as a divine title throughout Haggai (see 1:5, 7, 9, 14; 2:4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 23). This name (יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת, yehvah tsevaʾot), traditionally translated “Lord of hosts” (so KJV, NAB, NASB; cf. NIV, NLT “Lord Almighty”; NCV, CEV “Lord All-Powerful”), emphasizes the majestic sovereignty of the Lord, an especially important concept in the postexilic world of great human empires and rulers. For a thorough study of the divine title, see T. N. D. Mettinger, In Search of God, 123-57.

Heb “the time has not come, the time for the house of the Lord to be built” (similar KJV). A number of English versions refer to “rebuilding” (so NAB, NCV, NRSV, TEV, NLT, NIV11) since the reconstruction of Solomon’s temple is actually in view.

verses.zh: 那时耶和华的话临到先知哈该说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came through the prophet Haggai as follows:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the word of the Lord came by the hand of Haggai the prophet, saying.” Cf. the similar expression in v. 1 and the note there.

verses.zh: 「这殿仍然荒凉，你们自己还住天花板的房屋吗？
verses.en: “Is it right for you to live in richly paneled houses[NOTE:1] while my temple is in ruins?[NOTE:2]
notes: Richly paneled houses. Paneling is otherwise known in the OT only in connection with the temple (1 Kgs 6:9) and the royal palace (2 Kgs 7:3, 7). It implies decoration and luxury (cf. NCV “fancy houses”; TEV “well-built houses”; NLT “luxurious houses”). The impropriety of the people living in such lavish accommodations while the temple lay unfinished is striking.
Heb “Is it time for you, [yes] you, to live in paneled houses, while this house is in ruins”; NASB “lies desolate”; NIV “remains a ruin.”

verses.zh: 现在万军之耶和华如此说：你们要省察自己的行为。
verses.en: Here then, this is what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies has said: ‘Think carefully about what you are doing.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Set your heart upon your ways” (see 2:15, 18); traditionally “Consider your ways” (so KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB).

verses.zh: 你们撒的种多，收的却少；你们吃，却不得饱；喝，却不得足；穿衣服，却不得暖；得工钱的，将工钱装在破漏的囊中。」
verses.en: You have planted much, but have harvested little. You eat, but are never filled. You drink, but are still thirsty. You put on clothes, but are not warm. Those who earn wages end up with holes in their money bags.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Some translate “pockets” (so NLT) but the Hebrew word צְרוֹר (tseror) refers to a bag, pouch, or purse of money (BDB 865 s.v. צְרוֹר; HALOT 1054 s.v. צְרוֹר 1). Because coinage had been invented by the Persians and was thus in use in Haggai’s day, this likely is a money bag or purse rather than pouches or pockets in the clothing. Since in contemporary English “purse” (so NASB, NIV, NCV) could be understood as a handbag, the present translation uses “money bags.”

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：「你们要省察自己的行为。
verses.en: Moreover, this is what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies has said: “Pay close attention to these things also.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Set your heart upon your ways”; see v. 5.

verses.zh: 你们要上山取木料，建造这殿，我就因此喜乐，且得荣耀。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: Go up to the hill country and bring back timber to build[NOTE:1] the temple.[NOTE:2] Then I will be pleased and honored,”[NOTE:3] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “and build the house” (so NIV, NRSV), with “house” referring specifically to the temple here.
The temple was built primarily of stone, so the timber here refers to interior paneling (see v. 4) and perhaps to scaffolding (see Ezra 5:8; 6:4).

The Hebrew verb אֶכָּבְדָ (ʾekkavda) appears to be a defectively written cohortative (“that I may be glorified”). The cohortatives (note that the preceding אֶרְצֶה, ʾertseh, “I will be pleased,” may also be taken as cohortative) indicate purpose or result (cf. NIV, NRSV “so that”; CEV “so”) following the imperatives of v. 8a (“go up,” “bring back,” “build”).

verses.zh: 你们盼望多得，所得的却少；你们收到家中，我就吹去。这是为甚么呢？因为我的殿荒凉，你们各人却顾（原文是奔）自己的房屋。这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: “You expected a large harvest, but instead there was little.[NOTE:1] And when you would bring it home, I would blow it right away.[NOTE:2] Why?” asks the Lord of Heaven’s Armies. “Because my temple remains in ruins, thanks to each of you favoring his own house![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Turning for much—look! It is [become] little!” The term פָּנֹה (panoh) means “turning [the head],” and here it is in order to look around. The term הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) is an interjection drawing attention to the point being made.
Heb “I would blow at/against it.” The imagery here suggests that human achievements are so fragile and temporal that a mere breath from God can destroy them.
Heb “and each of you runs to his own house”; NIV “is busy with”; TEV “is busy working on”; NCV “work hard for.”

verses.zh: 所以为你们的缘故，天就不降甘露，地也不出土产。
verses.en: This is why the sky[NOTE:1] has held back its dew and the earth its produce.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text has “over you” (so KJV), but this is redundant in contemporary English and has been left untranslated.
This linkage of human sin to natural disaster is reminiscent of the curse brought upon the earth by Adam’s disobedience (Gen 3:17-19; see Rom 8:20-22).

verses.zh: 我命干旱临到地土、山冈、五谷、新酒，和油，并地上的出产、人民、牲畜，以及人手一切劳碌得来的。」
verses.en: Moreover, I have called for a drought that will affect the fields, the hill country, the grain, new wine, fresh olive oil, and everything that grows from the ground; it also will harm people, animals, and everything they produce.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all the labor of hands” (similar KJV, NASB, NIV); cf. NAB “all that is produced by hand.”

verses.zh: 那时，撒拉铁的儿子所罗巴伯和约撒答的儿子大祭司约书亚，并剩下的百姓，都听从耶和华―他们　神的话和先知哈该奉耶和华―他们　神差来所说的话；百姓也在耶和华面前存敬畏的心。
verses.en: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak,[NOTE:1] along with the whole remnant of the people,[NOTE:2] obeyed[NOTE:3] the Lord their God. They responded favorably to the message of the prophet Haggai, who spoke just as the Lord their God had instructed him,[NOTE:4] and the people began to respect the Lord.[NOTE:5]
notes: Many English versions have “Joshua [the] son of Jehozadak, the high priest,” but this is subject to misunderstanding. See the note on the name “Jehozadak” at the end of v. 1.

Heb “all the remnant of the people.” The Hebrew phrase שְׁאֵרִית הָעָם (sheʾerit haʿam) in this postexilic context is used as a technical term to refer to the returned remnant (see Ezra 9:14; Isa 10:20-22; 11:11, 16; Jer 23:3; 31:7; and many other passages). Cf. TEV “all the people who had returned from the exile in Babylonia.”
Heb “heard the voice of”; NAB “listened to the voice of.”

Heb “and according to the words of Haggai the prophet just as the Lord their God sent him.” Some English versions (e.g., NAB, NIV, NCV) take the last clause as causal: “because the Lord their God had sent him.”
Heb “and the people feared from before the Lord”; NASB “showed reverence for the Lord.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者哈该奉耶和华差遣对百姓说：「耶和华说：我与你们同在。」
verses.en: Then Haggai, the Lord’s messenger, spoke the Lord’s announcement to the people:[NOTE:1] “I am with you,” decrees the Lord.
notes: Heb “Haggai, the messenger of the Lord, said by the message of the Lord to the people.” The Hebrew is repetitive and has been simplified in keeping with contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 耶和华激动犹大省长撒拉铁的儿子所罗巴伯和约撒答的儿子大祭司约书亚，并剩下之百姓的心，他们就来为万军之耶和华―他们　神的殿做工。
verses.en: So the Lord energized and encouraged[NOTE:1] Zerubbabel[NOTE:2] son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak,[NOTE:3] and the whole remnant of the people.[NOTE:4] They came and worked on the temple of their God, the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: It was God who initiated the rebuilding by providing the people with motivation and ability.tn Heb “stirred up” (as in many English versions). Only one verb appears in the Hebrew text, but the translation “energized and encouraged” brings out its sense in this context. Cf. TEV “inspired”; NLT “sparked the enthusiasm of”; CEV “made everyone eager to work.”
Heb “the spirit of Zerubbabel” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest” (as in many English versions), but this is subject to misunderstanding. See the note on the name “Jehozadak” at the end of v. 1.

Heb “and the spirit of all the remnant of the people.” The Hebrew phrase שְׁאֵרִית הָעָם (sheʾerit haʿam) in this postexilic context is used as a technical term to refer to the returned remnant; see the note on the phrase “the whole remnant of the people” in v. 12.

verses.zh: 这是在大流士王第二年六月二十四日。
verses.en: This took place on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of King Darius’ second year.[NOTE:1]
notes: The twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of King Darius’ second year was September 21, 520 b.c., twenty-three days after the original command by Haggai to rebuild (1:1). The text does not state the reason for the delay, but it may have resulted from the pressing need to bring in the late summer harvest.
